clue.text: Refuse to accept a youngster carrying 12

indicators.note: the youngster carries the other answer inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, a youngster
the answer to 12 down, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take on a child who is lugging something around.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to the answer of 12 down, so its letters are borrowed from that clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an offer is to decline it, the phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Turned out, given direction, and took part

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
played means participated, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone was dismissed, told where to go, and joined in.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet or legs splayed are turned outwards, the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Frank condemnation of Tory policies?

explanation.surface: A blunt verdict on Conservative plans.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: being down on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means blunt and outspoken; read as 'down (on the) right' it is disapproval of right-wing policy.

clue.text: People one can threaten

parts.note: men means people, a body of persons
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain person is capable of intimidation.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace is to intimidate, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Surrounded and laid about a soldier king

indicators.note: the wager word is placed around the other pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: laid, as in laid a wager, means bet
a GI is an American soldier
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone was encircled and gambled on a royal fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid' is a past tense in the surface, but here it means placed a wager; GI is the usual American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Begirt is an archaic past participle of begird, meaning encircled as with a belt.

clue.text: Jocularity gets disagreeable in time

parts.note: bad means unpleasant or disagreeable
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Humour turns sour as the years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful banter, light jesting talk.

clue.text: Join and put in some hard work

explanation.surface: Attach and get stuck into a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft joins plant tissue or skin onto another; in British slang graft is also toil, to graft is to labour hard.

clue.text: Counted sapper drunk on deck

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer, of the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy army engineer is tallied on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper is a Royal Engineer, hence RE; 'drunk' is the anagram signal for ON DECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoned means calculated or tallied, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Plant Poles had demolished

indicators.note: demolished means knocked down, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people pulled down some building.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Further loan

explanation.surface: Lend more money.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a cause is to further it; an advance is money lent or paid early.

clue.text: Taking pains to adapt to the country

indicators.note: to adapt means to alter, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An immigrant tries hard to fit in with a new nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is an Iberian nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Bloomer made by people travelling by road?

definitions.text: Bloomer made by people travelling by road?

parts.words: Bloomer made by people travelling by road?
parts.note: a bloomer is a flower; split, the word suggests a whole nation of motorists

explanation.surface: A blunder committed by motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a pink flower, a bloomer in crossword terms; split, it is a 'car nation'.

clue.text: The dope used in America's such a problem

indicators.note: used in signals letters lodged within the following words

explanation.surface: Narcotics in the United States are a big problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a fool or idiot, as is this donkey word.

clue.text: The party leader lives for controls!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: resides means lives, dwells

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the head of the party is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair or be in charge, so to control proceedings.

clue.text: Greek state causing more anxiety

parts.note: aver means to state or assert

explanation.surface: A Greek nation causing increasing worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Graver means more serious, so giving more cause for concern.

clue.text: Give new order to the back row

parts.note: rear means the back
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Reorganise the seats at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put in a different sequence.

clue.text: Novelist made to turn in drink

indicators.note: in places the turning word inside the drinking word

parts.note: tope is an old verb for drink heavily
roll means turn over

explanation.surface: A writer was forced to rotate inside a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels, an example of a novelist.

clue.text: The rich holding of some woman

indicators.note: holding signals that the following words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: The wealthy own property belonging to a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Her is the female object pronoun, referring to some woman.

clue.text: Look on rambling roses as unattractive things

indicators.note: on places the first piece ahead of the second in this down answer

parts.note: to eye is to look at

indicators.note: rambling roses straggle, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gazing at untidy climbing roses as ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at.

clue.text: The prelacy view

explanation.surface: The bishops' outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese or office, the prelacy; to see is to view.

clue.text: Moderately appealing

explanation.surface: Somewhat attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means fairly, as in 'pretty good', and also attractive in appearance.

clue.text: Old man quite unaffected by retirement

indicators.note: retirement here means reading backwards; the word is unchanged when reversed

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A pensioner who is not bothered at all by giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for father.

clue.text: Dignity is just a joke in spring

indicators.note: in places the joking word inside the month

parts.note: May is a month in spring
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A claim that seriousness is merely a prank in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is stately grandeur, a synonym of dignity.

clue.text: Get close to a very quiet swimmer

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
a roach is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Sneak up softly on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach is to come near.

clue.text: Shoot the fellow going around double-parking!

indicators.note: going around means the first piece encircles the second

parts.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal

indicators.note: double asks for the parking abbreviation to be written twice over

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Gun down the man who keeps double-parking!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like an exclamation of annoyance at the parker, but it is the definition: to fire at.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper someone is to shoot them with many pellets or bullets.

clue.text: Keeping secret could mean chastisement

explanation.surface: Concealment might lead to a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding is concealing; a hiding is also a beating as punishment.

clue.text: Set against amalgamating, so leading

indicators.note: amalgamating mixes the words together, blending their letters anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Opposed to merging, so taking the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means placed beside, as one thing set against another.

clue.text: Currency no longer seen as superior

explanation.surface: Old money regarded as finer.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble was an old English gold coin, no longer used; noble also means lofty or high-ranking.

clue.text: Repair requiring half a day to complete

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is the morning half of the day
to end is to finish or complete

explanation.surface: A fix needing twelve hours to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to correct or put right.

clue.text: Held back for a wearying individual

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person

explanation.surface: Someone restrained themselves on account of a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbore, past of forbear, means refrained or held off.

clue.text: A number will stuff a bird to increase the size

indicators.note: stuff means fill, so the number is packed inside the bird

parts.note: a hen is a bird
eight is a number

explanation.surface: Cooking advice that stuffing a fowl makes it bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to make taller or greater.

clue.text: Gets even

parts.note: read as taking revenge, but meaning makes flat or equal

explanation.surface: Takes revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To level is to make flat or smooth, so to render even.
